label: October 2026 General Conference
subtitle: 196th Semiannual General Conference · 4 sessions · coded October 6, 2026
lead: Here is one careful answer: every talk summarized, the patterns we noticed across all 37, and everything we were explicitly asked to do, starting with President Oaks.
arc: 77% of the adversity material fell on Saturday; 90% of the truth-with-love material fell on Sunday.

notes.TH01: Covenants are described as acting when the person is not: ancestors' covenants reach a descendant raised elsewhere, and "covenants do not take a day off" (Morgan quoting Oaks). The protective claim runs both ways, for the wandering child and for the faithful spouse.
notes.TH02: The correction appears even inside a tithing talk ("This does not mean that we will be free from trials," Jufra). Matthew J. Eyring opened by naming Runia's "I can't fix this" from that morning, the weekend's clearest link between two talks.
notes.TH03: Grace works as connective tissue: the turn inside talks about adversity, wayward children, and teaching rather than a topic of its own. Runia's sculptor and Dunn's friend who quietly carried the pack make the same move: help resisted at first, then recognized.
notes.TH04: Failure is relocated from the outcome to quitting. Dube's story inverts the usual sequence: the couple set a sealing date before the husband had quit smoking. This theme maps most cleanly onto Theory of Trying.
notes.TH05: In every helping story the sequence is notice, then act: the frightened missionary at the airport, the janitor whose name was known, the child unbuttoning a sleeve. Two speakers cited the same Kimball line in one session, a notable convergence, though the transcript cannot show whether it was planned.
notes.TH06: The boundary arrives inside the same talk as the love. Folley warns against the lie that "because God loves us, we can be saved regardless of our pride," anticipating Sunday's truth-with-love ethic.
notes.TH07: Kungu's talk is the most operational in the corpus: one list of phrases to retire and one to use. Gilbert supplies the procedure (avoid contentious settings, find common ground, be a light, hold the truth, stay anchored in Christ) and models it with his own failure.
notes.TH08: Digital risk recurs across three sessions: mobile gambling (Christofferson), "artificial information" (Andersen), coarse online speech (Cook), sleep and phone limits (Muñoz Spannaus). Practices are the means, never the message, which is why the theme is broad but thin.
notes.TH09: Soares on fasting and Christofferson on gambling sat back to back on Saturday morning. Christofferson's is the only data-driven talk. The two tithing talks split the promise: Jufra stresses the faith test, Villanueva the discipline of noticing blessings already received.
notes.TH10: Witness runs from the top down (apostolic witness, a family that sailed through a storm to hear an apostle) and from the bottom up (a niece, a Primary child, a 25-minute Sunday School lesson). Oaks extends the invitation to all nations and frames grace as universal but conditional.

theory_note: Mapped after coding. Eleven of 25 thematic categories map to no construct; two are candidate contributions: covenant reach (a commitment acting on people who never made it) and God works through people (promised help delivered through third parties). Quality of theory use: applied (Painter et al., 2008).

design: What did the conference teach, how was it distributed across speakers and sessions, and what did speakers ask listeners to do?
Qualitative content analysis with thematic synthesis; descriptive claims only
Census of all 37 addresses by 36 speakers in four general sessions (44,044 words)
Transcript paragraph within an address (808 meaning units)
Two-cycle coding (Saldaña, 2013): 1,576 code applications, 124 codes, 26 categories, 10 themes
Single coder: an AI language model (Claude, Anthropic) following a written protocol
Segmentation manifest, range-coded assignments, codebook and log, memos, scripts
paragraphs: Machine (speech-recognition) transcripts of the four broadcast sessions. Speakers identified from conducting announcements and talk content; eight garbled names are marked with an asterisk. Sustainings, conducting remarks, prayers, and music excluded.

All 808 units read in full and coded in talk order, one to three codes each: Initial coding by default, In Vivo where the speaker's words carried the concept, Process coding for actions. A code was created only with a one-sentence definition and inclusion and exclusion rules. One analytic memo per talk.

Open, axial, and selective coding (Williams & Moser, 2019): codes grouped into 26 categories, then ten themes stated as claims. Constant comparison throughout. Rhetorical moves coded but held out of the themes. Theme count set by the principal investigator.

Pattern search for invitation language across all units, then a full reading of each talk's directive passages. Kept only items for members generally (subgroups flagged); promises excluded; each anchored to a verbatim quote.
Word counts, word frequencies, Christ-reference density, leader mentions, and recurring phrases produced by deterministic scripts. Scripture identified from the text by the coder.
trust: All 154 excerpts in the action list and example tables verified by script to appear word for word in the cited unit; transcription errors shown with bracketed corrections.
Rerunning segmentation reproduced all 808 units exactly; workbook counts are live formulas.
Codebook definitions, codebook log, and one memo per talk in the workbook.
Claims scoped to this conference; master codebook supports future comparison.
Blind double-code of one talk (17 units) prepared with Cohen's kappa; threshold 0.61 (Landis & Koch, 1977). Not yet completed.
method.reflexivity: Coding was performed by an AI language model working from the written protocol; the principal investigator set the scope and is responsible for reviewing the output. An AI coder is consistent and fully documented but can repeat a blind spot across passes, so a human double-code is required before publication.
limitations: Machine transcription garbles some names and words, so word counts are approximate.
Units follow transcript paragraph breaks, so some sentences are split.
Ten themes exceed the usual five to seven; themes 3 and 8 are broad but thin.
Theory mappings are cross-context and partly analogical (Venkatesh, Thong & Xu, 2016).
Single coder; agreement not yet measured.

steps: All 37 addresses from the four general sessions, from machine transcripts of the broadcast; speakers identified from the conducting announcements.
A manifest-driven script splits talks into 808 meaning units with stable IDs, so every claim can point to a unit.
Every unit read in full and given one to three codes (Initial, In Vivo, Process). A code exists only with a definition plus inclusion and exclusion rules.
Each new unit is compared with units already in its code; definitions are tightened, and merges and rule changes are logged.
Codes are grouped into categories (axial), then integrated into ten themes stated as claims (selective). Rhetorical moves are coded but kept out of the themes.
Every quotation is checked by script against the transcript; theory is consulted only after the themes exist; a blind double-code tests agreement.
method.saturation_note: All 26 categories had appeared by the 10th talk; after that, talks added new codes (talk-specific concepts) at a rate of 0 to 3 each but no new categories. The thematic structure was saturated well before the corpus ended (Guest, Bunce & Johnson, 2006).
method.standards: Reporting follows the Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research (O'Brien et al., 2014) and the relevant COREQ items (Tong, Sainsbury & Craig, 2007). Thematic synthesis follows Braun and Clarke (2006); reliability follows O'Connor and Joffe's (2020) guidance for intercoder agreement in qualitative research.

site.hero: What did they say in the last general conference?

five_min: Christ as the one who carries and lifts was the pattern we noticed in the most talks: 19 of 37.
Saturday dwelt on trials (77% of the adversity material); Sunday turned to how we treat each other (90% of the truth-with-love material).

President Oaks asked us to focus on developing faith in Christ, hold on to the first article of faith, keep our commandments and covenants, protect ourselves through the sacrament, believe the Book of Mormon's promises, act on and share these truths, and study the talks.
"Love" in its forms was spoken 270 times, nearly double "covenant" (148).

quiz.q: Which day carried most of the talk about trials and adversity?
quiz.why: 77% of the adversity material fell on Saturday.

quiz.q: Sister Runia said the gospel isn't the ___, it's the solid rock.
quiz.why: “The gospel isn't the umbrella, it's the solid rock we're standing on.”

quiz.q: Which word was spoken more often?
quiz.why: Love and its forms: 270. Covenant(s): 148. Temple(s): 78.

quiz.q: How many of the other 35 talks mentioned President Oaks?
quiz.why: He was mentioned in 19 and quoted in 14.

quiz.q: Which speaker made the case against gambling?
quiz.why: All 30 uses of “gambling” came from President Christofferson's talk.
